description:
Cut the seal over from the monolith to settled `RuntimeDemand(E)` facts, and delete the monolith path. This is blocked until `fz-rh2.29.5` proves equivalence at the transport projection boundary; raw `ExecutableRuntimeDemand` byte identity is not the right proof obligation.

## Change
1. Seal gathers `closure.runtime_demands` from settled `RuntimeDemand(E)` facts instead of `settle_runtime_demands`.
2. Seal sources latent executables from gathered `RuntimeDemand(E).callable_flows` using the existing demanded-callable executable rule. Discovery orchestration stays in the seal for now; only demand dataflow moves.
3. Remove shadow-only plumbing once the fact path is authoritative.

## Why
This is the actual runtime-demand win: the seal stops re-running whole-closure demand dataflow on every wake. Per-executable jobs re-derive from explicit fact dependencies. The cutover is safe only after the consumer-boundary projection proof exists, because internal value/call-arg provenance can differ without necessarily changing transport/codegen obligations.

## Sharp Edge Carried From T2
Before deleting the monolith, verify the authoritative fact path did not retain a hidden whole-closure base-demand decision. `base_return_demand` and `locally_called_executables` may disappear only because entry, caller, and boundary `ReturnDemand` contributions cover the same cases. If the cutover still needs a global locally-called set to decide whether an executable gets boundary demand, the fixpoint has not actually been dissolved.

## Rip Out
- `settle_runtime_demands` whole-closure driver.
- `base_return_demand`, re-expressed as contributions.
- monolith-only call-return and callable-boundary propagation once their contribution facts are authoritative.
- seal shadow-readiness checks that only existed while monolith output remained authoritative.

The reusable transfer helpers may stay if `DeriveRuntimeDemand(E)` is their sole caller.

## Check
`fz-rh2.29.5` is closed first. Then `cargo test --lib` and the fixture matrix pass with runtime demand sourced from facts. `rg` confirms the old monolith driver and global locally-called base-demand prepass are gone rather than orphaned. Update `.agent` docs and user-facing guides/northstar seal narrative to describe runtime demand as per-executable facts. Zero warnings; no scaffolding left behind.
title: Runtime demand: cut the seal over to the facts and strangle the monolith
